content: The effects of belladonna alkaloids can be enhanced by pharmacodynamic synergism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Phenobarbital and haloperidol both increase sedation, while belladonna alkaloids reduce haloperidol levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Belladonna alkaloids also reduce haloperidol levels through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Phenobarbital decreases haloperidol levels or effects by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Hawthorn increases the effects of phenobarbital through pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially enhancing central nervous system (CNS) depression. Caution and monitoring are advised. Belladonna alkaloids and henbane both reduce cholinergic effects or transmission, necessitating caution and monitoring. Phenobarbital reduces the effects of hemin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Drugs that increase delta-aminolevulinic acid synthetase may further decrease hemin efficacy. Caution and monitoring are required. Belladonna alkaloids and homatropine both reduce cholinergic effects or transmission, requiring caution and monitoring. Hops increase the effects of phenobarbital through pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially enhancing CNS depression. Caution and monitoring are advised. Huperzine A increases cholinergic effects, while belladonna alkaloids decrease them. The interaction's effect is unclear, so caution and monitoring are necessary. Phenobarbital reduces hydrocodone levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Discontinuing CYP3A4 inducers co-administered with hydrocodone may increase plasma hydrocodone concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Phenobarbital also reduces hydrocortisone levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Phenobarbital and hydromorphone both increase sedation, requiring caution and monitoring. Phenobarbital reduces hydroxyprogesterone caproate levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Hydroxyzine and phenobarbital both increase sedation, necessitating caution and monitoring. Belladonna alkaloids and hyoscyamine both reduce cholinergic effects or transmission, requiring caution and monitoring. Belladonna alkaloids and hyoscyamine spray also reduce cholinergic effects or transmission, necessitating caution and monitoring. Phenobarbital increases the effects of ifosfamide by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2B6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. Co-administration of ifosfamide with CYP2B6 inducers may increase its metabolism to active metabolites. Phenobarbital increases ifosfamide toxicity by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing the formation of neurotoxic or nephrotoxic metabolites like chloroacetaldehyde. Close monitoring for toxicities and dose adjustments are recommended. Iloperidone increases the effects of belladonna alkaloids through pharmacodynamic synergism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Belladonna alkaloids reduce iloperidone levels through pharmacodynamic antagonism and by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, which applies only to oral forms. Phenobarbital reduces iloperidone levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Phenobarbital reduces imatinib levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Belladonna alkaloids and imipramine both reduce cholinergic effects or transmission, requiring caution and monitoring. Phenobarbital reduces imipramine levels or effects by affecting CYP1A2, CYP2C19, and CYP3A4 metabolism. Phenobarbital and imipramine both increase sedation, necessitating caution and monitoring. Phenobarbital reduces indinavir levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are required. Belladonna alkaloids and ipratropium both reduce cholinergic effects or transmission. Due to poor systemic absorption of ipratropium, interaction is unlikely at recommended dosages. Phenobarbital reduces iptacopan levels or effects by increasing metabolism. CYP2C8 inducers may reduce iptacopan efficacy. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while isoproterenol decreases it. The interaction's effect is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. Phenobarbital reduces itraconazole levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Phenobarbital reduces ivermectin levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are required. Phenobarbital reduces ixabepilone levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ixekizumab may normalize CYP450 enzyme formation altered by chronic inflammation. Upon initiating or discontinuing ixekizumab in patients receiving CYP450 substrates, particularly those with a narrow therapeutic index, therapeutic effect monitoring is recommended. Kava increases the effects of phenobarbital through pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially enhancing CNS depression. Caution and monitoring are advised. Phenobarbital and ketamine both increase sedation, requiring caution and monitoring. Phenobarbital and ketotifen (ophthalmic) both increase sedation, necessitating caution and monitoring. Phenobarbital reduces labetalol levels by increasing metabolism. A higher beta-blocker dose may be needed during co-administration. Atenolol, sotalol, and nadolol are less likely to be affected than other beta-blockers. Phenobarbital reduces lamotrigine levels by increasing hepatic clearance. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Phenobarbital reduces lansoprazole levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Phenobarbital reduces lapatinib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are required. Phenobarbital and lasmiditan both increase sedation. Co-administration of lasmiditan with other CNS depressants, including alcohol, has not been clinically evaluated. Lasmiditan may cause sedation and other cognitive or neuropsychiatric adverse reactions. Caution and monitoring are advised. Phenobarbital and lemborexant both increase sedation. Dosage adjustment may be necessary if lemborexant is co-administered with other CNS depressants due to potentially additive effects. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Phenobarbital reduces lesinurad levels or effects by influencing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while levalbuterol decreases it. The interaction's effect is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. Phenobarbital reduces levamlodipine levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. No quantitative data are available on the effects of CYP3A4 inducers on amlodipine.
